idea-plugin.name: App Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
App Monitor turns the IDE into a live runtime dashboard for the apps you care about - independent of how they were started (IDE run config, terminal, docker, system service). Add an app by name + port and the panel shows its memory, CPU, listening ports, uptime and up/down status, refreshing automatically like docker stats.

Unlike a launcher, App Monitor tracks targets (a TCP port, a process name, a PID), not the process the IDE launched - so it can watch anything running on your machine. If an app is not found on a refresh it shows down, and flips back to up when it reappears.

MVP features:

  • Tool window with a live table: Name, Port(s), PID, Uptime, Status, Memory, Mem %, CPU %.
  • Add an app by port (optional: process-name / PID target, health URL, alert limits, tag).
  • Kill the process listening on a port (and its whole tree) - goodbye EADDRINUSE.
  • The list of monitored apps is persisted per project.
  • Works on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Spun off from the Multiple Run Monitor (part of the Multiple Run plugin).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0 (rich memory observability):

  • New: Mem trend sparkline per app (last minute of memory), red when climbing, green when flat/falling. Click it for the full chart.
  • New: full-session memory chart with labelled axes and the peak marked, a leak analysis (growth rate, per-hour projection, R², how often memory was never freed) and a verdict; export the history to CSV or the analysis to a report.
  • New: HTTP health check - set a health URL and the Status column refines to healthy/unhealthy (2xx/3xx = healthy), on top of up/down.

0.1.0 (MVP):

  • New: "App Monitor" tool window - add an app by port and watch its memory, CPU, ports, uptime and up/down status live, whatever launched it.
  • New: kill the process listening on a TCP port (whole process tree).
  • The monitored apps list is persisted per project. Linux, macOS and Windows.
